chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUbayd Allāh and ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said:
We asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who sleeps on his mount, and he said: If sleep takes away the intellect, then he must repeat the wudu (ablution).

key_terms.الرِّضَا عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: Imam al-Riḍā, the reported source of the ruling
key_terms.النَّوْمُ: sleep, specifically in its effect on consciousness
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purity state to be renewed
key_terms.يَنَامُ: sleeps; the act under discussion in the ruling

ai.seo_question: Does sleeping on one's mount invalidate wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding sleep and wudu (ablution). Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام states that when sleep overcomes a person to the extent that it removes awareness, the wudu (ablution) must be repeated.
